h1: Generators & Surge Protection in Broward County
intro: Protecting a South Florida home from outages and surges takes two layers: a standby generator and whole-home surge protection. Down here the power going out is not a rare event, it is part of life, and the same storms that knock out the grid send voltage spikes through it. A generator keeps your essentials on when the grid drops. Surge protection guards everything plugged into your wiring from the spikes that would otherwise damage it. Both are only as good as the electrical work behind them, so our licensed crew starts the same way every time. We look at your service in person, tell you plainly what it can support, and give you one honest price for the layer, or the layers, that fit your home.

definition.heading: What generators and surge protection do
definition.body: These are the two layers that keep a South Florida home steady through storm season, and they answer two different threats. A generator is a backup power source that keeps the power you depend on most running when the grid goes down. On its own it is just an engine and an alternator. What makes it safe and useful is the electrical work around it, especially a transfer switch that keeps generator power and grid power safely separated. Whole-home surge protection is a device installed at your electrical panel that guards your entire system against surges, the brief spikes in voltage that can damage or destroy what is connected to your wiring. Unlike a plug-in power strip that protects only the one thing plugged into it, a panel-mounted protector works at the source. One layer keeps the lights on when the grid fails, the other protects everything on your wiring from the spikes that arrive through it or start inside the home.

symptoms.title: Outages that keep leaving you in the dark
symptoms.body: The power goes out often enough that you have stopped being surprised by it. Each time you are counting hours and hoping it comes back before the food turns. A generator is how you stop living at the mercy of the grid.

symptoms.title: Medical equipment or a full freezer you cannot lose
symptoms.body: Someone relies on refrigerated medication or equipment that has to stay running, or a full refrigerator and freezer you cannot afford to lose. An outage stops being an inconvenience and becomes a real cost, and backup power is worth having before the next storm season.

symptoms.title: A house full of sensitive electronics
symptoms.body: Televisions, computers, a smart thermostat, kitchen appliances with circuit boards inside them. Modern homes are full of sensitive electronics, and a single surge can take out several at once. Protection at the panel guards all of it from one place.

symptoms.title: You have lost a device to a surge before
symptoms.body: Something in your home died suddenly and you never found out why. A surge is a common, invisible culprit. Once it has happened, most people decide they would rather protect the whole house than replace equipment one loss at a time.

symptoms.title: You are relying only on power strips
symptoms.body: Plug-in surge strips protect the one device plugged into them and nothing else, and they wear out quietly over time. If those strips are your only defense, most of your home, and its bigger equipment, is unprotected.

symptoms.title: A commercial property that cannot go dark
symptoms.body: Downtime costs your business real money, or your tenants expect the lights and systems to stay on. Commercial backup power and surge protection raise the same core questions as a home, at a larger scale, and both start with assessing the service.

process.title: The call and a few honest questions
process.body: You call and we talk about your property, your history with outages, and what you most want to keep running and protect. That conversation shapes everything that follows and tells you what to expect before we come out. No pressure, no script.

process.title: The on-site assessment
process.body: We come to the property and look at the electrical service, the panel, and the grounding your surge protection depends on, then work through what you want to keep powered. Sizing gets honest here. What a generator can carry depends on your service and the install, and we confirm that in person, not over the phone.

process.title: One honest price for the job that fits
process.body: From what we saw and what you told us, we forecast the work and give you one price for the layer, or layers, matched to your home. If the service or grounding needs attention first, we tell you plainly, once, and let you decide. We price it once and we price it right.

process.title: Our in-house crew does the install
process.body: Our own crew sets the generator and installs the transfer switch so grid power and generator power stay safely separated, and installs the surge protection at the panel with the grounding it relies on confirmed sound. The same people who priced the job do the work.

process.title: Permit, inspection, and a follow-up
process.body: This work is permitted and inspected, and we handle that. We pull the permit in our own name and we meet the inspector in person. Once it passes, we walk you through how everything runs and follow up so you know exactly what to expect the next time the grid goes down.

benefits.title: The essentials stay on
benefits.body: When the grid drops, the power you depend on most keeps running. Not a promise to run the whole house like nothing happened, but a real plan to keep what matters alive through an outage.

benefits.title: One line of defense for the whole home
benefits.body: Instead of protecting devices one strip at a time, a panel-mounted protector guards your entire electrical system from a single point, standing between your home and surges before they reach your outlets.

benefits.title: Tied in safely by a licensed crew
benefits.body: A transfer switch keeps generator power and grid power separated the way code requires, and surge protection is set on grounding we have confirmed is sound. This is exactly where a licensed install earns its keep.

benefits.title: Peace of mind before the next season
benefits.body: You stop dreading the forecast and the flicker of the lights. Knowing the essentials will stay on and your electronics are guarded is the quiet confidence these systems are really for.

localSections.heading: Heat, humidity, and hurricane season are the reason
localSections.body: The reason both of these matter here is the same reason South Florida is hard on equipment: the weather. Long, hot summers, heavy humidity, and a hurricane season that reliably tests the grid every year. Outages are simply a fact of life in this climate, and when they come they can last, which is what a generator is for. The same storm activity and the ordinary business of the grid also send surges down the line, on top of the small spikes your own air conditioning and pumps create every time they cycle. A generator installed here lives outdoors in heat and humidity and, near the coast, salt air, and the grounding that surge protection relies on corrodes in that same environment. That reality shapes how we do the work: proper connections, hardware suited to an outdoor South Florida location, and an install built to hold up season after season, not just to pass on day one.

localSections.heading: Older South Florida homes, service capacity, and grounding
localSections.body: Broward County homes come from many eras, and the electrical service in an older home was sized for the life that home was expected to live, not for a generator tied into it or a charger and appliances added decades later. A generator and its transfer switch are a meaningful addition, and they have to work with the service you already have. Surge protection has its own foundation question, because a protector depends on proper grounding to do its job, and homes wired decades ago were grounded to the standards of their day. Some panels and grounding are in fine shape. Others, especially the older problem-brand panels and corroded grounds found around South Florida, raise questions we answer before we promise anything. That is also why permitting matters. We pull the permit in our own name and meet the inspector in person, which protects you as the owner and leaves a clean record on the home, the kind of documentation a Florida carrier looks for at renewal or in a claim.

guide.title: The honest guide to storm-season power resilience in South Florida

sections.heading: Two layers: a generator and surge protection
sections.body: Protecting a home from power trouble down here really comes in two parts, and they solve different problems. The first is losing power altogether. Hurricane season tests the grid every year, summer storms knock out neighborhoods, and when an outage comes it can stretch from hours into days. A generator is how a household stops being helpless in that stretch. The second problem is the opposite: too much power, too fast. Surges are brief spikes in voltage that can damage or destroy the electronics tied into your wiring, and they arrive from the grid and start inside your own walls every time a large motor cycles on. A generator answers the first threat and surge protection answers the second. Most homes benefit from both, but you do not have to do both at once. We will tell you honestly which layer matters most for your home and let you decide the order, the same way we handle everything.

sections.heading: Standby generators: what the work really involves
sections.body: When people picture a generator, they picture the machine. The machine is the easy part. What makes a generator safe and genuinely useful is the electrical work that ties it into your home. A proper install connects the generator to your electrical system through a transfer switch, the device that keeps generator power and grid power completely separated so the two can never meet. If there is one part of a generator install you should never let anyone skip, it is that transfer switch. Without it, a generator can push power backward onto the utility lines, a condition called backfeed, which can injure or kill a lineworker who believes the line is dead and damage your own home when grid power returns. It is exactly why this work is permitted and inspected. It also means sizing the connection and the loads honestly, so the generator carries what you have chosen without being overwhelmed. For most homes a generator is not about running everything as if nothing happened. It is about keeping the essentials on: the refrigerator and freezer, medical equipment, the internet for a home office, a pump or a system that causes trouble the moment it stops. Deciding what counts as essential is one of the first conversations we have, because that answer shapes the whole install.

sections.heading: Whole-home surge protection and the grounding under it
sections.body: Whole-home surge protection is a device installed right at your electrical panel that guards your entire system from surges. The key word is whole-home. A plug-in power strip protects only the single device plugged into it. A panel-mounted protector works at the source, diverting the excess energy of a spike safely away before it can travel out to your outlets and everything on them. It surprises people to learn that many surges do not come from outside at all. They start inside the house, every time a large appliance with a motor, the air conditioner, a pool pump, a refrigerator, cycles on and off. Others arrive from the electrical service itself. A protector at the panel addresses that whole picture. It works best, though, on a foundation of proper grounding, which is the underlying safety system a surge protector relies on. Here is the honest frame, and it is the whole of it: if your house is grounded properly, it protects your family, it protects your investment, and it protects the home as a whole. That is the truth, and it is enough. We confirm the grounding is sound before we call the work done, because a protector on a poorly grounded home is only doing half its job.

sections.heading: Honest sizing and an honest word about cost
sections.body: This is the part where honesty separates a good installer from a salesperson, and it works the same way for both layers. What a generator can run is not a number we pull from a brochure. It depends on your electrical service, the install, and the specific loads you want to keep alive, so we assess your service in person and talk through your priorities before we promise anything. Surge protection depends on your panel and the condition of the grounding it will rely on. That is why both are quoted per property after an on-site assessment, and we do not publish a generator price, because an honest one does not exist until we have seen your service. For a straightforward install on a soundly grounded home, surge protection is one of the more affordable pieces of protection you can add. If you simply want us to come diagnose an existing electrical problem, our service call is 240 dollars, which covers roughly two hours including travel, arrival, and the diagnosis, and if the issue can be handled on the spot there is no separate return charge. If your service needs a full residential rebuild before either layer makes sense, that work runs in the range of 5,000 to 8,000 dollars. Price it once, price it right. That philosophy protects you from the surprises that come with a lowball number and a pile of change orders.

sections.heading: How to choose the contractor who installs it
sections.body: A generator and a surge protection system are serious additions to your home, and the electrical work behind them is what keeps them safe, so choose the installer with care. Ask whether they are licensed. Ghost Crown Electric is a Florida Certified Electrical Contractor with statewide authority and a Broward County Master Electrician, with 286 permitted projects on public record and ten years of showing up when we said we would. Ask whether they will pull a permit and have the transfer switch, the connection, and the grounding inspected, because anyone willing to skip that is skipping the part that keeps these systems from becoming a danger. Ask whether they will actually check your grounding rather than just bolt a device onto the panel and leave. Ask who does the work, an in-house crew or a rotating set of subs. And listen for honesty about sizing and about your service, because an installer who will tell you the truth about what a generator can and cannot carry is one who will be honest with you about everything else. We stay in our lane, we do the work right, and we let a decade of doing it that way speak for us.

faqs.question: What can a generator actually run in my home?
faqs.answer: That depends on your electrical service, the install, and the loads you choose to keep on, which is why we assess it in person before promising anything. For most homes a generator is about keeping the essentials alive, the refrigerator, medical equipment, internet, key systems, rather than running the entire house. We tell you honestly what a given setup will and will not carry.

faqs.question: Why does the transfer switch matter so much?
faqs.answer: The transfer switch keeps your home drawing from either the grid or the generator, never both. Without it, a generator can push power back onto the utility lines, which can injure a lineworker who thinks the line is dead and damage your own home when grid power returns. It is the single component that makes backup power safe, and we never shortcut it.

faqs.question: What does whole-home surge protection actually protect?
faqs.answer: It guards your entire electrical system and the equipment tied into it, from televisions and computers to appliances with circuit boards inside them. Installed at the panel, it stands between your home and surges before they reach your outlets. Unlike a plug-in strip that covers only one device, a panel-mounted protector is the first line of defense for the whole house at once.

faqs.question: Where do surges even come from?
faqs.answer: Many start inside your own home. Every time a large appliance with a motor cycles on and off, the air conditioner or a pool pump, it creates a small spike in your electrical system. Others arrive from the electrical service as the grid delivers power and utility equipment switches. Surge protection at the panel addresses the whole picture, the spikes from outside and the ones that begin in your walls.

faqs.question: How much does this cost?
faqs.answer: Both layers are quoted per property after an on-site assessment. We do not publish a generator price, because an honest one does not exist until we have seen your service and understood what you need to keep running. Surge protection on a soundly grounded home is one of the more affordable protections you can add. If you want us to diagnose an existing problem first, the service call is 240 dollars, roughly two hours including travel, arrival, and diagnosis.

faqs.question: Do you install for commercial properties?
faqs.answer: Yes, for both homes and commercial properties across Broward County. A commercial job raises the same core questions as a home, whether the service can support the system and what has to stay running or be protected, just at a larger scale. We assess the property in person, forecast the work, and give you one honest price quoted for your specific building.
